rows.ARS:
Light pink Floribunda.
Registration name: PROberg
Exhibition name: Pink Iceberg ™
rows.Origin:
Discovered by Lilia Margaret Weatherly (1927-2012) (Australia, 1991).
Introduced in United States by Weeks Wholesale Rose Grower, Inc. as 'Pink Iceberg'.
Introduced in Australia by Swane's Nursery/Swane Bros Pty Ltd in 1997 as 'Pink Iceberg'.
rows.Bloom: Pink. Sometimes white. Mild fragrance. 35 petals. Average diameter 4". Large, full (26-40 petals), in small clusters bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Few or no prickles/thorns. Glossy, light green foliage.

Height: 2' (60cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).

Variety: Pink Iceberg

Breeders' code: Proberg

Trade reference: Blushing Pink Iceberg

A spontaneous mutation seen on a large so-called climbing 'Iceberg' (8') in 1991. Propagated by Lilia Weatherly in Tasmania and subsequently budded by John Nieuwesteeg in Victoria.

Flowers vary in colour from white to mainly pink (RHS Colour 65A-D), with great variation in between, often looking 'hand-painted'. Sometimes a single petal will be sharply divided into white and pink down the mid line. Some inflorescences show white and pink flowers side by side United States - Patent No: PP 9,600 on 9 Jul 1996 VIEW USPTO PATENT

Floribunda rose plant named Proberg

Lilia M. Weatherly, Tasmania, Australia

... pink blush flowers... discovered as a mutation in a controlled planting of the variety known as 'Iceberg'... The delicate shades of pink of the petals produce what has been described as a "hand painted" look... Average bloom size when fully expanded -- about 3 inches... Number of petals under normal conditions -- about 35... Fragrance: Slight... Hips: Urn shape... Height attained: About 2 feet... Resistance to disease: Blackspot -- Excellent. Mildew -- Excellent. Rust -- Excellent... Winter hardy in Australia...
